solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fantastic Lakeland after leaving large area somewhere in Cumbria

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and unreal, so the remaining letters are rearranged
once things have left, they are no longer there, so the named pieces are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for large
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A tourist raves about the Lake District after leaving a big stretch of the county for some Cumbrian spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one L and one A out of LAKELAND and rearrange the KELAND left over. Kendal is a market town in Cumbria, on the edge of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendal is a real town in the county of Cumbria, so it is one particular place there.

clue.text: Thrill over support for illegal payment

parts.note: a kick is a buzz of excitement
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone gets a thrill from propping up a corrupt bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' just puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickback is a bribe paid secretly in return for a contract or favour.

clue.text: Supposed citizen having love for Austria

indicators.note: 'having one thing for another' means a swap: the first goes in where the second was

parts.note: a national is a citizen of a country
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: An alleged citizen is said to have a love for Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the first A of NATIONAL with O to get NOTIONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means existing only in theory or imagination, which is what supposed can mean.

clue.text: Ambassador interrupting middle of game? It's said to gain attention

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so one piece sits inside another
only the central part of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the two central letters of the word game
His (or Her) Excellency is an ambassador's title, abbreviated HE

explanation.surface: An ambassador breaks into the middle of a match, asking whether that's the way to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole sentence after the question mark: a polite cough is something said to get attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The throat-clearing interjection is uttered to catch someone's notice or signal mild disapproval.

clue.text: A special thing that might be tapped around house plant

indicators.note: something placed around another surrounds it, so the pair of pieces wraps the next one

parts.note: taken as written
SP is a standard abbreviation for special
HO is the abbreviation for house
the delete key on a keyboard, labelled Del, is something you tap

explanation.surface: A special object you might tap on, sitting around the home, turns out to be a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces from 'special thing that might be tapped' sit either side of the house. The asphodel is a lily-like flower of Mediterranean origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a flowering species of the lily family, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Second work? Cite this possibly when entertaining a refined type

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: to entertain is to host a guest, so one piece is held inside another
'possibly' says the words are one possible version of the letters, so they are reordered

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
taken as written, ready to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A second piece of writing: perhaps quote this when hosting a cultured guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the musical opus abbreviation; the single A is held inside the rearranged pair of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophisticate is a worldly, cultivated person, which is what a refined type is.

clue.text: Pay attention to the educational hosts

indicators.note: a host holds a guest within, so the phrase contains the answer inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary of the two words

explanation.surface: Listen to the educational establishments that welcome visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles tHE EDucational.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to take notice of something, as in heeding a warning.

clue.text: Daughter has saunter with time gone and walk in the park?

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: something gone is no longer present, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: to toddle is to stroll in a leisurely way
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A daughter strolls along, losing track of time, and takes a walk in the park.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from TODDLE and put D in front. 'Walk in the park' looks literal but is the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both doddle and 'walk in the park' are informal idioms for a task that is very easy.

clue.text: See director, say, turning up with right person for a short stay?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters are written from bottom to top

parts.note: 'say' gives EG (for example), attached to D for director
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Spot a film director, perhaps, arriving with the proper guest for a brief visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director, say' reads as 'for example, director', so the abbreviation for 'for example' comes first before the turn. The question mark admits a lodger's stay need not be short.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger pays to live in someone else's home, usually for a limited time.

clue.text: Mess left exposed in coastguard's vessel

indicators.note: the letter is left exposed in the sense of being cast out, so it is taken away

parts.note: clutter is an untidy mess
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Untidiness is left lying around on a coastguard boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the L out of CLUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutter is a small fast boat of the kind used by coastguards and revenue services.

clue.text: Excellent supply in food for parties on the counter

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
counter means opposite, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: dips such as hummus are typical party food
to lend is to supply or provide

explanation.surface: A great stock of party nibbles is laid out on the kitchen counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' paints a kitchen worktop but means read backwards, as counter means against or opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid is an enthusiastic word for something very fine or impressive.

clue.text: Inspector stuck with a pair of fellows in part has resentment

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a section is a part of something
taken as written
F is fellow, so two of them is FF

explanation.surface: A police inspector saddled with two colleagues in one division feels bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' puts the article and both fellows inside the word for part, with the inspector in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Disaffection is discontent with those in authority, a feeling of resentment and estrangement.

clue.text: Favour singer Pat on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the answer is about how a name sounds

parts.note: Pat Boone was an American pop singer of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A listener requests a song by Pat Boone on a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer's surname sounds the same without its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or a favour granted, as in asking a boon of someone.

clue.text: Restriction found in slim item

indicators.note: what is found in a phrase is sitting inside its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A constraint is discovered in a thin object.
explanation.walkthrough: It sits in sLIM ITem.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or cap placed on something, which is a restriction.

clue.text: On and off, Celt uses hint

indicators.note: on and off means switching between taking and skipping, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Now and then, a Celtic person makes use of a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep C, L, U, E from CeLt UsEs.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a piece of evidence or a pointer toward a solution, a hint.

clue.text: Gaudy poster not seen in dark?

indicators.note: what is not seen in a word is missing from it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: shadowy means dark and dim
an ad is an advertisement, like a poster

explanation.surface: A garish placard that cannot be seen in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaudy poster' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Gaudy'; remove AD from SHADOWY.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy means flashy and attention-seeking, which is what gaudy describes.

clue.text: They are first picked up in English city

indicators.note: picking up a sound means hearing it, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: those who are first are in the lead; they are the leads

explanation.surface: The front runners are collected in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major city in West Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: A companion with role that is dividing island groups on tour?

indicators.note: something dividing another splits it in two, sitting between its halves

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island
taken as written
CH is a Companion of Honour
a part in a play is a role
ie stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A travelling partner with a job splits a cluster of islands on a holiday trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island groups' looks like archipelagos, but only 'island' is wordplay; 'groups' belongs to the definition. Cos is the Greek island also spelt Kos.
explanation.definitionFit: Coach parties are groups of people travelling together on a coach, typically on an organised tour.

clue.text: Put down tips for leisure in Surrey town writer disowned

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
what is disowned is cast off, so it is dropped from the word

parts.note: Reigate is a town in Surrey, south of London
the writer of a clue refers to themselves as I

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word leisure

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a Surrey town after collecting some advice on free time.
explanation.walkthrough: Reigate is a commuter town in Surrey, south of London; the writer of a clue is I, and losing that leaves room for the tips.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to demote or consign to a lower rank, which is to put someone down.

clue.text: Particular European institute found in varied places

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: what is found in something sits inside it
varied means altered, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
I is the abbreviation for institute

explanation.surface: A specific European institution has branches in many locations.
explanation.walkthrough: PLACES rearranges to SPECAL, I goes inside, and E leads off.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is a formal adjective for something particular or exceptional, as in especial care.

clue.text: Tenor with a few seconds broadcast showing insincerity

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenor whose brief moment on air reveals him to be a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-facedness is duplicity, showing one face while hiding another, which is insincerity.

clue.text: What cuts weight when promoted creates interest

indicators.note: a piece that cuts another goes into the middle of it
promoted means raised, and in a down entry a raised word reads upward

parts.note: flab is excess body weight
eh is a way of saying what? when you have not heard

explanation.surface: Something that slashes weight on being promoted generates interest.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the weight is promoted; 'what' stays as written and cuts in. The definition fits through 'in the interest of' and 'on behalf of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on someone's behalf means acting in their interest, so the noun stands for interest or benefit.

clue.text: Pressure on mad rogue operator

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
mad in the sense of angry

explanation.surface: Pressure is put on a furious, crooked businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on' puts the P above IRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is an unlicensed operator, such as a pirate radio station or someone copying goods illegally.

clue.text: Chinese leader is among French and making departure

indicators.note: being among things means sitting in their midst, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: et is French for and
Xi Jinping is China's leader

explanation.surface: China's leader mixes with the French on his way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese leader' looks like the first letter of Chinese, but it is the president's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a way out or the act of leaving, which is a departure.

clue.text: Severe sign of austerity in site with many patients?

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: A&E is a hospital's Accident and Emergency department, full of patients
spending cuts are the mark of austerity

explanation.surface: Budget cuts at a busy hospital department are harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency room; CUT goes between its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute describes a severe, intense condition, such as an acute shortage.

clue.text: Dog in part of Liverpool lacking sun

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so that letter goes

parts.note: Speke is a district of Liverpool, home to its airport
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: A dog in a gloomy part of Liverpool gets no sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S from SPEKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peke is a Pekingese, a small long-haired breed of dog.

clue.text: Touched soft material

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of feel, to handle
second meaning: a fabric of matted wool

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as stroking some fabric; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of the verb meaning to touch and a pressed woollen fabric.

clue.text: Announce cut for item

indicators.note: to announce is to say out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut

explanation.surface: Declare a price reduction on a product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' is the informal word for a romantic couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who are 'an item' are a pair, romantically linked.

clue.text: Not directly useful description of some research?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of theoretical interest only
second meaning: relating to scholarship and universities

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a sly dig at research; the word that means scholarly also means of no practical relevance.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both scholarly, as university research is, and irrelevant in practice, as in 'the point is academic'.

clue.text: This person's upset about a rule in African country

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other
something upset is turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: this person is the speaker, so 'this person is' is I'M
taken as written
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A speaker is angry about one regulation in an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person's' is short for 'this person is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked country in southeastern Africa.

clue.text: Temporary set of cars in capital of Guyana

parts.note: a company's fleet is its set of vehicles
taken as written

indicators.note: a capital is a head or upper-case initial, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Guyana

explanation.surface: A fleet of cars is used briefly in Georgetown, Guyana's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing cars in a city, but it supplies its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeting means passing quickly, lasting only a short time, so it is temporary.

clue.text: Soldiers have treatment for harrowing experience

parts.note: OR means Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
a deal is the way someone is treated, as in a raw deal

explanation.surface: Troops receive medical care after a terrible time in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful, prolonged trial that is distressing to go through.
